quotes: **Reputation track and display:** whenever you increase reputation, advance your counter 1 step. Reaching a space with a bonus grants that bonus immediately, once. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (reminder icon on space 10 / folder 5). If your counter is on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take **1 appeal per remaining reputation step**. "Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. After a turn in which display cards were taken: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

requestedparts.part: Build I permits exactly one building no larger than strength
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size no greater than strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical in one action. Buildings cost 2 money per space. First building must touch at least one map border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by an edge. Build on empty map spaces only, not beyond map or over buildings, water or rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. New kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately gives +1 appeal once.

quotes: - **Side I:** Build **exactly 1 building** of your choice, of size up to the action's strength. Pay **2 money per space** (cost = size × 2) into the supply before placing. Available: kiosk (size 1), pavilion (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (special enclosure, size 3; maximum 1 per zoo — other buildings can be built more than once).

quotes: - **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

quotes: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. requestedparts.part: Task strengths are reputation two, partner three, university four and conservation five
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, conservation work 5. Side I performs exactly one task; Side II can perform one or more different tasks whose total values do not exceed action strength. Workers are required for tasks: if one of yours is already on that task, place 2 workers; if three are there, you cannot repeat it until after break. Other players' workers do not matter.

quotes: - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

- **Gain partner zoo (strength 3):** take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty partner-zoo space of your map (take any printed bonus immediately). All your partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum 4 total; the third (or fourth) requires the upgraded Association action. If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.

- **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space (take any printed bonus; advance your Reputation counter if the university shows it). You cannot take a duplicate university. Universities grant reputation and research icons and are the only way to increase your hand limit to 5.

- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). The Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved, even when fully supported, and no new base projects are added during the game.

requestedparts.part: A new project must be played and supported immediately
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: At Association strength 5, support a project already in play or play a hand Conservation Project and support it immediately; Side II also allows a new card from the in-range display for folder-number cost. New project goes above the Association board, leftmost, pushing others right. To support, meet an unoccupied condition level and place one of your map-edge conservation-support tokens on it; each level holds one token total across players, and you normally may support a given project only once. Taking the token activates its map bonus, before or after project reward at your choice. If card count exceeds player-count limit (2/3/4 cards), discard rightmost and return tokens on it to owners' supplies; already activated bonuses stay activated.

quotes: - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). The Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved, even when fully supported, and no new base projects are added during the game.

- **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

quotes: - **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.

- To **support** a project: fulfill a condition on the card that has no player token on it, and place 1 player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition. You may support each project only **once** (never one already holding your token). As a reward, advance your Conservation counter (and Reputation counter, if shown) per the depicted award. If you fulfill several conditions, you choose one. Taking a token off your zoo map activates its bonus — gained immediately, and for some bonuses again in each break; you choose whether to take it before or after the project reward.

requestedparts.part: Use printed standard-size bands: two-minus accepts one/two, three accepts three, four-plus accepts four/five
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: No. Release size bands are 2− = printed standard size 1 or 2, 3 = size 3, 4+ = size 4 or 5. Lose only the animal's printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard it and lose its icons, but retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects. New Release project play gives 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not. To free housing, if the animal can use a special enclosure and its indicated tokens can be removed, you must remove them; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, else smallest meeting size alone, else none. Actual tile or special-enclosure capacity does not determine release size.

quotes: - **Release into the wild** projects work differently: instead of counting icons, discard 1 Animal card with the specific icon from your zoo; match the animal’s **printed standard-enclosure requirement to the depicted size category**: **2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts size 3; 4+ accepts size 4 or 5**. You cannot use an animal from another category. The actual enclosure tile occupied, or capacity in a special enclosure, does not define this category. First lose only the animal's printed appeal, **before** gaining conservation points; discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. If the animal could live in a special enclosure and its indicated number of special-enclosure tokens can be removed, you **must remove those tokens**; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure. Flip the smallest occupied standard meeting all requirements, else the smallest meeting size alone, else none if no occupied enclosure meets size. This applies even to flock animals. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants 1 reputation; supporting one already in play does not.

quotes: **End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. **Your zoo map:** buildings go in the large central area. You may not build on rock and water spaces (some animals need an enclosure next to rock or water). A built-on space is "covered." Spaces with a special icon may not be built on until you upgrade your Build Action card. Some spaces show a **placement bonus**, gained immediately when you cover them. The left edge holds the 7 player tokens used to support conservation projects (each grants a bonus when taken — always immediately, and some again in each break). The bottom has 5 card slots for your Action cards; the number above each slot is that card's strength. The right side has spaces for partner zoos (5 continents exist, but you can partner with a maximum of 4 — the third requires an upgraded Association action) and universities (3 different ones); fill each column bottom-up and take any bonus printed on a space you cover immediately. Workers, money, and X-tokens live on the notepad.

quotes: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.

requestedparts.part: Donation requires Association II
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Side II permits exactly 1 donation per Association action, only after at least one task; donation needs no worker. Pay the smallest amount still visible, cover that space with one of your supply player tokens, and gain 1 conservation. Printed costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then the repeatable 12-money space; skip setup-blocked spaces. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no further token. The summary does not enumerate any additional donation conditions.

quotes: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. When doing conservation project work you may also play the new Conservation Project card directly **from the display** (within reputation range, paying the folder number as an additional cost; no replenish until turn end). In addition you may make exactly **1 donation**: pay the smallest amount of money still visible in the donation area, cover that space with a player token from your supply, and gain **1 conservation point**. The printed donation costs are **2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10**, then the repeatable **12-money** space; skip spaces blocked at setup. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each subsequent donation costs **12 money** (no further tokens placed). A donation requires having performed at least 1 association task in the same action, needs no worker, and is limited to 1 per Association action.

requestedparts.part: Upper-right Animal and Sponsor icons count
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: Zoo icons are upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards, partner-zoo and university icons, and upper-left water/rock requirements. Left-side conditions and Conservation Project icons do not count. A card counts its own icons for its effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Card text takes priority over general rules.

quotes: - **Icon-count** projects: count the icons on the top edge of all your cards — Animal and Sponsor (including the water or rock space requirements, but not the conditions on the left side) — plus your partner zoos and universities. The card itself counts for its own effects; a double icon counts twice. Conservation-project icons do not count as icons in your zoo. Breeding Program projects (123–127) have the same requirement for all three reward spaces: choose any available one.

Card text takes priority over general rules. Cards count their own icons for instant effects and recurring triggers. Only upper-right card icons, partner-zoo/university icons and upper-left water/rock requirements count as zoo icons; left-side conditions and conservation-project icons do not. Doubled icons count twice and trigger matching effects twice. Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes: touching one water hex in a larger water area gives one adjacency; several edges touching that hex still give only one. Water/rock illustrations on tiles provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements.

quotes: 3. **Fill an empty enclosure:** any animal except Petting Zoo animals can go on its own into an empty **standard enclosure** of at least the required size (hexagon number); flip the enclosure to its occupied side. requestedparts.part: Another herbivore with at least the flock animal's printed size avoids flipping new enclosure
requestedparts.evaluation: The answer supplies this requested meaning and the frozen summary supports it.
requestedparts.observedanswerquote: A flock animal avoids a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least its printed standard-enclosure size. That same host herbivore can host any number of flock animals. Without a qualifying herbivore, house it normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join its enclosure. On release, no proof of original accommodation is tracked; releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under release/fallback procedure.

quotes: - **Flock Animal:** if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size, you need not flip an empty enclosure. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. Releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure even if the flock animal originally shared. Exact historical residents are not tracked.

- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action.
